extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (healthcare providers, insurers, Exchanges), State regulators, policy analysts, and stakeholders affected by HHS Section 1557 rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory analysis for implementing and assessing HHS's final rule under Section 1557 (nondiscrimination in health programs), including amended nondiscrimination language, enforcement/authority clarifications, and the Regulatory Impact Analysis assumptions and cost estimation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded definition of sex for nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the term “sex” with the phrase “sex (including discrimination on the basis of sex characteristics, including intersex traits; pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity; and sex stereotypes).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change is applied across multiple regulations (45 CFR 147.104(e), 155.120(c), 155.220(j), 156.125(b), 156.200(e), and 156.1230(b)). The preamble repeats that these amendments prohibit discrimination on the basis of sex in the conduct of health insurance issuers and their officials, employees, agents, and representatives; States and the Exchanges; agents, brokers, or web-brokers; issuers subject to EHB requirements; and QHP issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments do not mandate coverage of particular services
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendments we are finalizing ... do not require regulated entities to cover any particular service not already covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the rule prohibits discrimination in the provision of health services, it does not compel covered entities to offer or cover specific treatments (e.g., gender-affirming care). To the extent an entity provides a service, it must provide it in a neutral, nondiscriminatory manner consistent with the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: State enforcement authority and reliance on statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: States have primary enforcement authority over issuers for regulations implementing title XXVII of the PHS Act; section 1557 is not codified in title XXVII so PHS Act section 2723 does not provide States authority to enforce section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS relies on its authorities under sections 2702 and 2792 of the PHS Act when amending 45 CFR 147.104. Though States do not enforce the administrative procedures specified in the section 1557 regulation itself, States may utilize independent enforcement authorities to pursue violations of law by entities within their jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom/conscience balancing (substantial burden and least restrictive means)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the prohibition imposes a substantial burden on an entity's exercise of religion and whether it is the least restrictive means of advancing the government's interest will depend on specific facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department allows entities to seek assurance of protections for religious freedom and conscience rights (see § 92.302). Determinations about substantial burden and least restrictive means are fact-specific and may include consideration of less restrictive alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 12866 significant regulatory action criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A “significant regulatory action” is any action likely to result in a rule that may: (1) have an annual effect on the economy of $200 million or more (adjusted every 3 years); (2) create a serious inconsistency or interfere with another agency action; (3) materially alter budgetary impacts of programs; or (4) raise legal or policy issues for which centralized review would further the President's priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department treats this final rule as a significant regulatory action under EO 12866 (as amended by EO 14094) and therefore conducts the relevant regulatory review and analyses required by EO 12866 and related Executive Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) small-entity impacts requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Flexibility Act requires analysis of regulatory options that would minimize any significant impact of a rule on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Department determined the costs of the final rule are small relative to revenue of covered entities, it certified that the final rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; the RFA analysis and supporting assumptions are documented in the RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act applicability and exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 202(a) requires a written statement assessing anticipated costs and benefits for any rule including any Federal mandate that may result in expenditures of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This final rule is not subject to the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act because it falls under an exception for regulations that establish or enforce statutory rights that prohibit discrimination on grounds such as race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, or disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: E.O. 13132 federalism analysis requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 13132 establishes requirements when promulgating rules that impose substantial direct costs on State and local governments, preempt State law, or have federalism implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department determined the final rule would not significantly affect the rights, roles, and responsibilities of the States and documents that conclusion in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) major rule thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: CRA defines a “major rule” as one likely to result in (A) an annual effect on the economy of $100,000,000 or more; (B) a major increase in costs or prices; or (C) significant adverse effects on competition, employment, investment, productivity, or ability to compete internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on its analysis under EO 12866, the Department expects this rule to qualify under 5 U.S.C. 804(2)(A) and will comply with CRA notification requirements to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA cost categories to quantify
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2016 RIA identified five sources of monetized costs: training and familiarization, enforcement, notice publication, sex discrimination policy and procedure changes, and language access plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final RIA quantifies costs associated with training employees, revising policies and procedures, notices (Notice of Nondiscrimination and Notice of Availability), documenting training activities, and incremental costs associated with coverage for gender-affirming care (although coverage is not mandated). It also separately reports ranges of total cost estimates using 3% and 7% discount rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline scenario assumptions (carry forward prior-rule impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline scenario of no further regulatory action is informed by prior RIAs (2016 and 2020) and includes ongoing costs attributable to prior rulemaking, such as enforcement and ongoing training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RIA adopts previous assumptions where appropriate (e.g., enforcement costs estimated in 2016 RIA adopted as baseline) and updates data (e.g., covered entity counts) where newer sources are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered-entity population and firm-size data updating
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the number of covered entities and number of covered entities with 15 or more employees using the latest available data (e.g., SUSB 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final RIA updates the prior count (275,002) to 266,297 total entities and revises the number with 15+ employees to 63,950; cost calculations use these updated counts and NAICS-based identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training cost estimation methodology and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume a share of employees receive one-hour training; use occupation categories, employment counts, and average fully loaded wage rates to monetize time costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This final RIA assumes 75% of employees at covered entities (14.2 million of 18.9 million total employees) receive one hour of training; computes weighted fully loaded hourly wage ($65.41) and estimates first-year training costs (~$927.3 million). The RIA documents the five occupation categories, employment counts, and average loaded wages used in the calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity and alternative-scenario analysis for training
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct sensitivity analyses such as assuming training for all employees versus only those interacting with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A scenario training all 18.9 million employees increases first-year training cost to about $1.2 billion; the RIA notes possible overstatement if training replaces existing training and that offsets may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing training incremental estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate ongoing annual training costs by taking the difference between baseline and final-rule shares of employees receiving training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a baseline assumption that 50% received training and final-rule assumption that 75% receive training, the RIA takes 25% of total employees (incremental) and multiplies by the weighted fully loaded wage to estimate ongoing annual training costs (~$309.1 million).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator training one-time cost assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR assumes 91 investigators (GS-12 Step 1 equivalent) will receive a one-time 8-hour training during the first year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using an average loaded hourly wage of $65.46, the total cost for this training is estimated at $47,655 (91 x 8 x $65.46). This training is assumed not to recur in subsequent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising policies and procedures cost methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate per-entity time spent revising policies: entities with more extensive revisions spend 4 total hours (3 by mid-level manager, 1 by executive); less extensive revisions use 2 total hours (1 mid-level manager, 1 executive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fully loaded hourly rates for mid-level managers ($62.98) and executives ($118.14) to monetize time; compute per-entity costs ($307.08 for extensive; $181.12 for less extensive) and aggregate across covered-entity counts to derive total costs (~$40.8M and $24.1M respectively for half/half split).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices and taglines cost estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify costs associated with notices (Notice of Nondiscrimination and Notice of Availability) and taglines; OCR derives monthly notice costs ranging from $21.28 to $26.60 per entity depending on prevalence of electronic delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments reporting different cost estimates (e.g., $8.91/month or larger insurer estimates) were considered; OCR reconciles commenter-provided estimates with its analysis, noting averages and entity-size variation. Notice costs are included in the RIA and sensitivity discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic discrimination inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a specific provision on algorithmic discrimination and qualitatively discuss the potential costs to individuals from discriminatory application of algorithms and decision support tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR qualitatively discusses potential costs and includes algorithmic discrimination considerations as part of benefits and potential unquantified costs in the RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to estimating incremental costs for gender-affirming care
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate incremental costs associated with coverage for gender-affirming care using peer-reviewed sources and actual cost data (e.g., NEJM article, Defense Manpower Data Center), while noting the rule does not mandate coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA quantifies a range of total costs that include possible incremental costs for gender-affirming care but emphasizes low utilization and specialist supply constraints that limit aggregate impacts; comments about long-term costs without supporting data were not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing assurance-of-exemption requests and documentation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate one-time costs to covered entities to process assurance of exemption requests and costs associated with documenting training activities required under the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RIA includes one-time processing costs and ongoing administrative/documentation burdens related to the rule as part of the quantified and unquantified costs.
